newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: SLOVAK GVT APPROVES DRAFT LAW ON EXCESSIVE IMPORTS.
newsitem.headline: SLOVAK GVT APPROVES DRAFT LAW ON EXCESSIVE IMPORTS.

text.p: The Slovak government on Tuesdsay approved a draft law to protect Slovak producers against excessive imports in a further step to help curb its trade deficit.

"The law will adjust legislation to protect domestic producers against excessive imports of goods which can endanger their production," Economics Minister Karol Cesnek told journalists after a regular cabinet session.

Cesnek said the law, which still needs parliamentray approval, would enable the state to impose "emergency measures" when imports of specific products might damage local industry producing similar goods.
He did not specify the measures or the goods which would be affected by the new law.

"These (restrictive) measures could be imposed only on the demand of producers accounting for at least 50 percent of Slovak production," Cesnek said. It could take up to nine months for the measures to be introduced.
Cesnek said the government expected all members of the World Trade Organisation (WTO) to accept the new Slovak law when approved by parliament, saying it was fully in line with WTO principles.

Slovakia's trade deficit totalled 15.894 billion crowns in the first three months of this year, up from 10.82 billion in the January-February period and compared with a 15.440 billion crown in the January-March period of 1996.
Government officials, including Cesnek, have repeatedly said they expect the full year 1997 deficit to stay around the level of last year's shortfall of 64.54 billion crowns.
